context:
Goal: you can always undo a recent action, and no control shows that does nothing.
Problem (rule): your pick c on item 193 shows Recent while anything can be undone, "also right after a Reset". But a Reset is not a Recent row, and it deletes the cards, so every row goes dead and the cell hides right after a Reset. Undoing a Reset needs the saved copy from before the Reset, and the record forbids a Recent undo to use it.
Based on (ruling): item 193 pick c (12:36 CST Nov 6): "Show while anything can be undone".
Based on (read): recent-checks-can-be-undone: a Reset is not logged, and "An undo never ... restores a snapshot" (main 5014f6f).
Based on (read): src/app.jsx:3954 saves a copy before every Reset, and History can restore it today.
Departs from: recent-checks-can-be-undone (an undo never restores a saved copy) — option a lets one Recent row, the Reset row, restore the copy saved before the Reset.
Meanwhile: the lane lands the item-193 rewrite as a draft record PR that says the Reset case is open.

options.gain: The undo shows right after a Reset, when you need it, in one tap.
options.how: Log a Reset as a Recent row whose undo restores the copy saved before the Reset.
options.label: Reset gets a Recent row
options.lose: One exception to "an undo never restores a saved copy". That undo also rolls back anything done after the Reset, so the row goes dead after your first new action.

options.gain: Recent keeps one simple rule: every undo is a small new write.
options.how: History stays the way to undo a Reset.
options.label: Keep Reset out of Recent
options.lose: Right after a Reset, Recent hides and you must open History to undo it, which is not what pick c promised.

short: mailaudit: undo a Reset from Recent?
title: mailaudit: can a Reset be undone from the Recent list?
why: a keeps pick c's promise: the undo is there right after a Reset.
